newsitem.title: FINLAND: SAK, STTK SAY RESOLUTION HELPS THEM DECIDE ON EMU.
newsitem.headline: SAK, STTK SAY RESOLUTION HELPS THEM DECIDE ON EMU.

text.p: The leaders of Finlad's two biggest trade union groups said on Thursday that a resolution on EMU signed by them and employers marked a step towards helping the unions support Finnish membership of the single currency.

"In the eyes of the STTK chairman, we took one step closer to a positive stance (on EMU)," Esa Swanljung, chairman of the over 600,000-member Confederation of Salaried Employees (STTK), told a news conference.

Lauri Ihalainen, chairman of the 1.1-million member Central Organisation of Finnish Trade Unionms (SAK), said "certain goals were now accomplished", but other issues still needed to be resolved, the most important being buffer arrangements.
"Neither Lauri Ihalalainen nor SAK have yet decided on EMU," he said. An agreement on some kind of buffers in case of severe external shocks was "absolutely essential," he said.

Political analysts have said the trade unions' views on Finnish EMU membership will be crucial for many left-wing members of parliament. The legislature is scheduled to vote on the issue early in 1998.
Openly pro-EMU Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen's social democratic parliamentary group is believed to be divided on EMU membership.
SAK's council is due to decide its stance on EMU in November.
